content.title: Multiple sidebar switches keep one-page state
content.intent: Prove repeated sidebar changes across primary, analytics, research, and system contexts keep the dashboard in the same single-page shell while the active item and workspace heading update in place.
content.technique_notes: Applied state / flow and negative reasoning to the source's forbidden routing promise across a multi-hop navigation sequence. Used representative section switching instead of all permutations because the outcome is the same single-page in-place update for each hop. Risk-gated covering strength was 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss factor applies; no covering array was needed for this single dominant sequence path.

content.title: Keyboard navigation changes dashboard context in place
content.intent: Prove the sidebar can be operated by keyboard so a focused navigation item becomes active and updates the workspace heading without leaving the current page.
content.technique_notes: Applied the a11y technique because the product requires keyboard operation, visible focus, and accessible headings on rendered surfaces. Chose one representative keyboard-driven context change because the behavior outcome matches pointer-driven activation across items. Risk-gated covering strength was 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss factor applies; no covering array was needed.

content.title: Default workspace opens with Overview active
content.intent: Prove the dashboard shell starts with the full sidebar inventory visible, Overview selected by default, and the initial workspace heading already aligned to that default context.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to the fixed sidebar inventory and default-state promises on initial load. This path covers the one-time initial shell state rather than an interaction combination, so no covering array was needed. Risk-gated covering strength was 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss factor applies.

content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to the PRIMARY family by choosing one non-default representative item with the same expected single-page outcome as the other PRIMARY targets. judgements.rationale: [value_score] Ranked highest because repeated switching is the quickest way to expose hidden routing, stale heading updates, or active-state drift across section boundaries while still staying close to the source-defined navigation promise.
[value_score] Ranked second because keyboard operation is explicitly required by the source accessibility rules and directly affects whether this navigation use-case is reachable for keyboard users.
[value_score] Ranked next because the default Overview state anchors the shell before any interaction and exercises most fixed-sidebar presence promises in one path.
[value_score] Ranked above the other representative section clicks because PRIMARY holds the default and most common top-level dashboard movement from Overview into another main context.
[value_score] Ranked after PRIMARY because ANALYTICS is a major context family whose click behavior should match the primary shell contract.
[value_score] Ranked after ANALYTICS because RESEARCH uses the same shell behavior but is slightly less central to the workspace entry flow than PRIMARY and ANALYTICS.
[value_score] Ranked after RESEARCH because SYSTEM has the fewest items and the same shell behavior, so one representative click completes family coverage at lower incremental risk.
